title: Up to 3.2x Faster Inference with LFM2.5-DSpark
summary: The article introduces DSpark, a speculative decoding technique for the LFM2.5 family of models (1.2B-Instruct, 2.6B, and 8B-A1B), which significantly accelerates inference speeds without compromising output quality. DSpark achieves up to 3.18x throughput improvement on GPUs and up to 2.87x on-device (e.g., M4 Max MacBook). The method combines parallel backbone processing, a lightweight sequential head, and a confidence-scheduled verifier to optimize token acceptance rates. The draft models are small (~300M parameters) and support frameworks like llama.cpp and SGLang. Benchmark results show consistent speedups across datasets, with notable latency reductions for function-calling tasks.
key_points: DSpark is a speculative decoding technique for LFM2.5 models, offering up to 3.2x faster inference on GPUs and on-device hardware without altering output quality.
The method uses a lightweight draft model (~300M parameters) to generate candidate tokens, verified by the target model in a single forward pass, reducing memory-bound latency.
Three components of DSpark: parallel backbone (DFlash-style), sequential Markov head for inter-token dependency, and confidence-scheduled verifier for pruning low-confidence tokens.
Benchmark results show significant throughput improvements: e.g., LFM2.5-2.6B achieves 140+ tokens/s on a MacBook, surpassing many proprietary cloud models.
DSpark reduces function-calling latency by 57% on average for LFM2.5-2.6B and supports frameworks like llama.cpp and SGLang with open-source integrations.
Draft models are available in Safetensors and GGUF formats on Hugging Face, with day-one support for Metal kernels and experimental optimizations.
